questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: What is the tunica adventitia?
questions.modelAnswer: The tunica adventitia is the outer connective-tissue coat of a vessel. It contains mainly type I collagen with variable elastic fibers, fibroblasts, nerves, lymphatics, and—in larger vessels—vasa vasorum, and it anchors the vessel to surrounding tissue.
questions.explanation: A complete answer should identify the relevant microscopic structures and connect each structural feature to its function in cardiac muscle, blood vessels, capillaries, or lymphatics.
questions.keyConcept: Accurate cardiovascular histology depends on relating microscopic organization to mechanical, conductive, exchange, or drainage function.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Why are large arteries called elastic or conducting arteries?
questions.modelAnswer: They are called elastic because their media contains numerous elastic lamellae that stretch during systole and recoil during diastole. They are conducting arteries because they carry blood away from the heart and smooth pulsatile ventricular output into more continuous flow.
questions.explanation: A complete answer should identify the relevant microscopic structures and connect each structural feature to its function in cardiac muscle, blood vessels, capillaries, or lymphatics.
questions.keyConcept: Accurate cardiovascular histology depends on relating microscopic organization to mechanical, conductive, exchange, or drainage function.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Why are medium-sized arteries called muscular or distributing arteries?
questions.modelAnswer: Their media is dominated by circumferential smooth muscle, so they are muscular arteries. By contracting or relaxing this muscle, they regulate lumen diameter and distribute blood selectively to different organs.
questions.explanation: A complete answer should identify the relevant microscopic structures and connect each structural feature to its function in cardiac muscle, blood vessels, capillaries, or lymphatics.
questions.keyConcept: Accurate cardiovascular histology depends on relating microscopic organization to mechanical, conductive, exchange, or drainage function.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Why are vasa vasorum needed in large and medium-sized vessels?
questions.modelAnswer: The walls of large vessels, and some medium vessels, are too thick for luminal diffusion alone to nourish the outer media and adventitia. Vasa vasorum supply these outer layers, while the inner wall is nourished mainly by diffusion from the lumen.
questions.explanation: A complete answer should identify the relevant microscopic structures and connect each structural feature to its function in cardiac muscle, blood vessels, capillaries, or lymphatics.
questions.keyConcept: Accurate cardiovascular histology depends on relating microscopic organization to mechanical, conductive, exchange, or drainage function.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: 36-year-old male suffered from diabetes mellitus with decrease in his metabolic exchange. Examination of his kidney, retina and skin show some structural changes. Which of the following structures is most likely affected?
questions.explanation: Diabetic microangiopathy classically thickens the capillary basal lamina in the kidney, retina, and skin, impairing normal metabolic exchange across the capillary wall.
questions.keyConcept: Diabetic microangiopathy thickens the capillary basal lamina.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: A 60-year old man diagnosed as having an atheroma. Which of the following structures of his blood vessel is most likely affected?
questions.explanation: Atheroma formation begins as lipid and cellular accumulation within the subendothelial connective tissue of the tunica intima, forming the fibro-fatty plaque.
questions.keyConcept: Atheroma originates in the subendothelial connective tissue of the intima.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: A 60-year-old man is diagnosed as having atherosclerosis. He is a heavy smoker. His clinical examination reveals hypertension. His lab test shows hyperlipidemia. Which of the following structures could be detected in L/M examination of his arterial wall?
questions.explanation: Atherosclerosis in a patient with hyperlipidemia, hypertension, and smoking classically shows fatty (atheromatous) plaque deposits within the arterial intima on light microscopy.
questions.keyConcept: Atherosclerosis shows fatty plaque deposits in the arterial wall.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: A case of atheroma, in which of the following cells the fat droplets accumulates?
questions.explanation: In atheroma, macrophages phagocytose lipid and become lipid-laden foam cells, the classic cellular hallmark of early atherosclerotic plaque.
questions.keyConcept: Macrophages become lipid-laden foam cells in atheroma.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: A case of atheroma, which of the following fibers are increased?
questions.explanation: Atherosclerotic plaques show increased deposition of collagen fibers as part of the fibrous cap that forms over the lipid core.
questions.keyConcept: Atheroma plaques show increased collagen deposition (fibrous cap).

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Absence of internal elastic lamina is a character of which of the following blood vessels?
questions.explanation: The metarteriole, being essentially a discontinuous smooth muscle coat around an endothelial tube, lacks an internal elastic lamina, unlike conducting arteries, medium arteries, basilar artery, and most arterioles which possess one.
questions.keyConcept: Metarterioles lack an internal elastic lamina.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Aging is accompanied by thickening of the wall of the blood vessels. Which of the following types of collagen are most likely increased?
questions.explanation: Age-related thickening and stiffening of the vessel wall is associated with increased deposition of type I and type III collagen, the principal fibrillar collagens of the vascular wall.
questions.keyConcept: Vascular aging increases type I and III collagen deposition.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: All of the following characterizes the blood capillaries EXCEPT:
options: Conduct blood from metarterioles to venules
questions.explanation: Capillaries are indeed thin-walled, extensively branching tubes of endothelium that link metarterioles to venules, but they are typically accompanied by pericytes, not devoid of them, making that the exception.
questions.keyConcept: Capillaries are usually accompanied by pericytes, not pericyte-free.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: All of the following characterizes the E/M of the endothelium of blood capillaries EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Capillary endothelial cells show short microvilli, numerous pinocytotic vesicles, scattered mitochondria, and cytoskeletal desmin/vimentin filaments, but they lack organized myosin filaments (a feature of contractile cells like pericytes/smooth muscle, not endothelium).
questions.keyConcept: Endothelial cells lack myosin filaments (unlike contractile pericytes).

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: All of the following features characterizes sinusoidal capillaries EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Sinusoidal capillaries have an irregular, wide lumen, a discontinuous endothelial wall, a discontinuous or absent basement membrane, and a reticular fiber-supported wall, but they characteristically lack pericytes, unlike continuous capillaries.
questions.keyConcept: Sinusoids typically lack pericytes.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Arterio-venous shunt is characterized by which of the following?
options: Pass directly from arterial to venous side
Pass directly from venous to arterial side
Pericytes are enclosed within the basal lamina
questions.explanation: Arteriovenous anastomoses are direct communicating channels that shunt blood from the arterial side straight into the venous side, bypassing the capillary bed entirely.
questions.keyConcept: AV shunts bypass capillaries, connecting arterial flow directly to veins.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Arterioles differ from medium-sized arteries in which of the following?
options: Few smooth muscle fibers in subendothelial layer
Prominent and wavy internal elastic lamina
Adventitia half the thickness of the media
questions.explanation: Arterioles lack the external elastic lamina found bordering the media of medium-sized (muscular) arteries, and have far fewer medial smooth muscle layers and a thinner, less wavy internal elastic lamina.
questions.keyConcept: Arterioles lack an external elastic lamina, unlike medium-sized arteries.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Basilar artery differs from coronary artery in which of the following?
options: Its media contains two elastic laminae
Monocytes and fat droplets in its intima
questions.explanation: Unlike the coronary artery (whose media has two elastic laminae), the basilar artery lacks an external elastic lamina altogether.
questions.keyConcept: Basilar artery lacks an external elastic lamina, unlike coronary arteries.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Basilar artery is similar to a vein in which of the following?
options: Adventitia is as thick as the media
Media is thin with little elastic fibers
questions.explanation: Despite being an artery, the basilar artery has a comparatively thin wall, resembling the thin walls typical of veins.
questions.keyConcept: Basilar artery resembles veins in having a thin wall.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Basilar artery is similar to an artery in which of the following?
options: Adventitia is as thick as the media
Media is thin with little elastic fibers
questions.explanation: A well-developed internal elastic lamina is the clearly arterial feature of the basilar artery. Its relatively thin wall and wide lumen are more vein-like, while its media remains smooth-muscular but contains relatively little elastic tissue.
questions.keyConcept: Paired basilar-artery comparison question; answer per source key.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Blood sinusoids are characterized by all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Show wide intercellular clefts between endothelial cells
questions.explanation: Sinusoids have a discontinuous (not continuous) basement membrane along with fenestrated endothelium, wide intercellular clefts, and a wider caliber than ordinary capillaries, all of which favor bulk exchange of cells and large molecules.
questions.keyConcept: Sinusoids have a discontinuous basement membrane, not a continuous one.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Blood sinusoids are present in all of the following organs EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Sinusoidal capillaries are characteristic of bone marrow, spleen, and liver, where slow, wide-channel blood flow supports cell filtering/exchange, but the small intestine is supplied by fenestrated capillaries, not sinusoids.
questions.keyConcept: The small intestine has fenestrated capillaries, not sinusoids.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Blood sinusoids of the bone marrow are characterized by which of the following?
options: Have no or discontinuous basement membrane.
questions.explanation: Bone marrow sinusoids have an irregular, wide lumen with a discontinuous endothelium and little or no basement membrane, an arrangement that allows newly formed blood cells to pass directly into the circulation.
questions.keyConcept: Bone marrow sinusoids have a discontinuous or absent basement membrane.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Bone marrow is characterized by the presence of which of the following vessels?
questions.explanation: Bone marrow is vascularized by wide, irregular sinusoidal capillaries with a discontinuous wall that allows mature blood cells to enter the circulation; bone marrow notably lacks lymphatic capillaries altogether.
questions.keyConcept: Bone marrow is supplied by sinusoidal capillaries and lacks lymphatics.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Conducting arteries differ from muscular arteries in which of the following?
options: Few amounts of elastic lamina in the media
The tunica intima constitutes 20% of the media.
Tunica intima consists of endothelial cells.
questions.explanation: In elastic (conducting) arteries such as the aorta, the tunica intima is proportionally thicker, reaching about 20% of the thickness of the media, compared with the much thinner intima of muscular (distributing) arteries.
questions.keyConcept: Elastic arteries have a proportionally thicker intima than muscular arteries.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Direct connection of arterio-venous anastomosis differs Glomus in which of the following?
options: Its arteriole has no internal elastic lamina
questions.explanation: A simple direct arteriovenous anastomosis is a single vessel connecting artery to vein, whereas the glomus (glomus body) is a more elaborate structure formed of three distinct vascular segments (arterial, intermediate, venous) enclosed in a connective tissue capsule.
questions.keyConcept: Simple AV anastomoses are single vessels; glomus bodies have three segments and a capsule.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Endothelial cells of the intima of aorta are joined by:
questions.explanation: Aortic endothelial cells are joined by tight (occluding) junctions, which help maintain the selective permeability barrier of the vessel lining.
questions.keyConcept: Endothelium is joined by tight junctions.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Fenestrated blood capillaries are present in which of the following combinations of organs?
questions.explanation: Fenestrated capillaries, with pores that permit rapid exchange of fluid and small molecules, are typical of the kidney (glomerulus), intestinal mucosa, and endocrine glands, in contrast to the continuous capillaries of skin, brain, and skeletal muscle.
questions.keyConcept: Kidney, intestine, and endocrine glands share fenestrated capillaries.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Glomus is present chiefly in which of the following sites?
questions.explanation: Glomus bodies (specialized arteriovenous anastomoses with a capsule) are concentrated in the skin of the fingers and toes, where they help regulate heat loss.
questions.keyConcept: Glomus bodies are concentrated in the digits (fingers/toes).

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Inferior Vena Cava (IVC) differs from radial veins in which of the following?
options: Longitudinally arranged smooth muscle fibers in adventitia
Numerous vasa vasorum in tunica adventitia
questions.explanation: The IVC is distinguished by longitudinally arranged bundles of smooth muscle fibers within its thick adventitia, a feature not shared with smaller peripheral veins such as the radial vein.
questions.keyConcept: IVC adventitia contains longitudinal smooth muscle bundles.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Internal elastic lamina shares in the nourishment of the wall of the blood vessels due to:
options: Its location close to the lumen of the blood vessel.
Its location close to the sub-intimal connective tissue.
questions.explanation: The perforations (fenestrae) in the internal elastic lamina allow nutrients from the lumen to diffuse through to the otherwise avascular inner media.
questions.keyConcept: Fenestrae in the internal elastic lamina permit nutrient diffusion to the inner media.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: L/M examination of a blood vessel wall formed of single layer of endothelium with few pericytes enclosed by the basal lamina, which of the following blood vessel most likely has this character?
questions.explanation: Post-capillary venules resemble capillaries structurally, consisting of endothelium with only a few scattered pericytes sharing the basal lamina, and lack a true smooth muscle coat.
questions.keyConcept: Post-capillary venules resemble capillaries with only scattered pericytes.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: L/M examination of cerebral capillaries of the blood brain barrier shows all of the following structures EXCEPT:
options: Endothelial cells are joined by tight junctions
Endothelial cells show very few pinocytotic vesicles.
Pericytes enclosed within the basal lamina
questions.explanation: Blood–brain barrier capillaries have continuous endothelium joined by tight junctions, a continuous basement membrane, pericytes, and very low vesicular transport. A discontinuous basement membrane is therefore the single exception.
questions.keyConcept: Blood-brain barrier capillaries have a continuous basement membrane, not a discontinuous one.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: L/M examination shows a blood vessel and its wall is formed of a single layer of endothelium with numerous pericytes and thin adventitia, which of the following blood vessel most likely has this character?
questions.explanation: Collecting venules are larger than post-capillary venules and show endothelium surrounded by numerous pericytes plus a thin adventitial layer, but still no organized smooth muscle media.
questions.keyConcept: Collecting venules show numerous pericytes and a thin adventitia.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Large lymphatic vessels are similar to veins in all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Formed of 3 tunicae; intima, media & adventitia
Media is formed mainly of smooth muscle fibers.
questions.explanation: Large lymphatic vessels resemble veins in having three tunicae, a media of smooth muscle, an adventitia thicker than the media, and no elastic laminae, but they possess far more numerous internal valves than veins, which is the exception.
questions.keyConcept: Large lymphatic vessels have far more internal valves than comparable veins.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Lymphatic capillaries are characterized by which of the following?
questions.explanation: Fibrillin-rich anchoring microfibrils tether lymphatic endothelial cells to surrounding connective tissue and help keep blind-ended lymphatic capillaries patent as interstitial pressure rises.
questions.keyConcept: Elastin anchoring filaments keep lymphatic capillaries open.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Lymphatic vessels are found in all organs EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The central nervous system parenchyma lacks conventional lymphatic vessels, unlike the kidney, liver, skin, and intestine, which all contain lymphatics (bone marrow also lacks them).
questions.keyConcept: The CNS parenchyma lacks conventional lymphatic vessels.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Medium sized artery differs from medium sized vein in which of the following?
options: Thin media with few elastic fibers
The media shows external elastic lamina
questions.explanation: Medium-sized arteries have a thick muscular media bordered by a well-developed external elastic lamina, a feature that medium-sized veins (thin media, no external elastic lamina) lack.
questions.keyConcept: External elastic lamina is present in medium arteries but absent in medium veins.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Metarteriole differs from arteriole in which of the following?
options: Discontinuous smooth muscle fibers of the media
questions.explanation: Unlike the continuous smooth muscle layer of arterioles, the metarteriole has a discontinuous smooth muscle coat that forms precapillary sphincters regulating flow into individual capillaries.
questions.keyConcept: Metarteriole media has discontinuous smooth muscle forming precapillary sphincters.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Metarteriole is a transitional vessel between:
questions.explanation: The metarteriole is the transitional segment linking the terminal arteriole to the true capillary network, regulating blood flow into capillary beds via precapillary sphincters.
questions.keyConcept: Metarteriole bridges arteriole and capillary networks.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: On examination of the wall of the blood vessels of 80-year-old women shows thickening of the wall with less flexibility. Which of the following structures are most likely affected?
questions.explanation: Age-related loss of vessel wall flexibility with thickening reflects changes in the extracellular fiber matrix — increased/altered collagen (types I and III) and reticular fibers along with degeneration of elastin — rather than the cellular components listed.
questions.keyConcept: Vessel wall stiffening with age reflects altered collagen, reticular, and elastic fiber content.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Pericytes differ than endothelial cells in which of the following?
options: Rests on its own basement membrane
questions.explanation: Pericytes characteristically express contractile/cytoskeletal proteins including desmin and vimentin, whereas endothelial cells chiefly express vimentin. Pericytes are embedded within the vascular basement-membrane compartment rather than resting on a separate, independent basement membrane.
questions.keyConcept: Pericytes rest on their own basal lamina, distinct from endothelium.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Regarding glomerular capillaries, all of the following are true EXCEPT:
options: Have a continuous, thick basement membrane
Fenestrae are closed by a diaphragm
questions.explanation: Adult glomerular capillaries are fenestrated and have a thick, continuous glomerular basement membrane; blood arrives through the afferent arteriole. Their endothelial fenestrae generally lack diaphragms, so the statement that the fenestrae are closed by a diaphragm is the exception.
questions.keyConcept: Glomerular capillaries are fenestrated yet retain a thick, continuous basement membrane — the key filtration barrier.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Small arterioles are characterized by:
options: Diminished smooth muscle fibers in terminal arterioles
questions.explanation: As arterioles taper toward terminal arterioles, the number of smooth muscle layers in the media progressively diminishes, down to a single discontinuous layer at the terminal arteriole/metarteriole level.
questions.keyConcept: Smooth muscle content diminishes toward terminal arterioles.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Smooth muscle cells in the tunica media is responsible for the secretion of all of the following EXCEPT?
questions.explanation: Vascular smooth muscle cells of the media synthesize elastin/elastic lamellae, type III collagen, and proteoglycans, but type I collagen is chiefly produced by fibroblasts in the adventitia, not by medial smooth muscle.
questions.keyConcept: Medial smooth muscle makes elastin/type III collagen; type I collagen is mainly adventitial.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: The distal segment of the arterio-venous shunts is similar to which of the following vessels?
questions.explanation: The distal (efferent) segment of an arteriovenous shunt drains into and resembles a venule in structure.
questions.keyConcept: Distal segment of an AV shunt resembles a venule.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: The intermediate segment of the arterio-venous shunts is characterized by which of the following?
options: Found only in lips, tongue and toes
questions.explanation: The intermediate (middle) segment of an arteriovenous shunt has a thick, well-developed muscular media that, under autonomic control, regulates whether blood is shunted directly or diverted through capillaries.
questions.keyConcept: Intermediate AV-shunt segment has a well-developed, autonomically controlled media.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: The proximal segment of the arterio-venous shunts is similar to which of the following vessels?
questions.explanation: The proximal (afferent) segment of an arteriovenous shunt resembles a small muscular arteriole in its wall structure.
questions.keyConcept: Proximal segment of an AV shunt resembles an arteriole.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: The two semilunar folds of the venous valves are located at which of the following sites?
questions.explanation: Venous valves are semilunar folds of the tunica intima (endothelium plus a core of connective tissue) that project into the lumen to prevent retrograde flow.
questions.keyConcept: Venous valves are folds of the tunica intima.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Thoracic duct and right lymphatic duct are similar to large veins in all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Formed of 3 tunicae; intima, media & adventitia
Media is formed of smooth muscle fibers.
questions.explanation: Unlike large veins, the thoracic duct and right lymphatic duct actually have a relatively thick (not thin) adventitia; they otherwise share three tunicae, no elastic laminae, vasa vasorum, and a smooth-muscle media with large veins.
questions.keyConcept: Thoracic/right lymphatic duct adventitia is thick, unlike large veins.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Thoracic duct and right lymphatic duct differ from large veins in which of the following?
options: Formed of 3 tunicae; intima, media & adventitia
Media is formed of bundles of circular and longitudinal smooth muscle fibers.
questions.explanation: The media of the thoracic duct and right lymphatic duct is distinctively organized into bundles of both circular and longitudinal smooth muscle fibers, a more complex arrangement than the media of large veins.
questions.keyConcept: Thoracic/right lymphatic duct media has both circular and longitudinal smooth muscle bundles.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Tunica adventitia of coronary arteries contains which of the following?
questions.explanation: The adventitia of coronary arteries contains longitudinally arranged bundles of collagen fibers, distinct from the monocytes, fat droplets, and elastic laminae found in the intima and media.
questions.keyConcept: Coronary artery adventitia contains longitudinal collagen bundles.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Tunica adventitia of medium-sized arteries differs from tunica media in which of the following:
options: It forms about half thickness of the media
It does not contain elastic fibers.
It contains circularly arranged smooth muscle fibers
questions.explanation: In medium-sized (muscular) arteries the adventitia is typically about half as thick as the media and, unlike the media, does not contain circularly arranged smooth muscle; it does carry lymphatics, nerves, and vasa vasorum.
questions.keyConcept: Medium artery adventitia is roughly half the thickness of the media.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Tunica media of coronary arteries contains which of the following?
questions.explanation: Unlike typical muscular arteries with a single internal elastic lamina, the coronary artery media is distinguished by containing two elastic laminae in addition to smooth muscle.
questions.keyConcept: Coronary artery media contains two elastic laminae.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Vasa vasorum of IVC is located at which of the following site?
questions.explanation: The vasa vasorum supplying the IVC's thick wall are located in the outer part of the tunica adventitia, from where they penetrate inward.
questions.keyConcept: IVC vasa vasorum are found in the outer adventitia.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which basement-membrane feature distinguishes lymphatic capillaries from blood capillaries?
questions.explanation: Lymphatic capillaries have a discontinuous (or absent) basal lamina, unlike the continuous basal lamina typically found around blood capillaries, which helps them readily take up interstitial fluid and macromolecules.
questions.keyConcept: Lymphatic capillaries have a discontinuous basal lamina, aiding fluid uptake.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which endothelial feature distinguishes lymphatic capillaries from blood capillaries?
questions.explanation: Lymphatic capillary endothelial cells overlap in flap-like folds that act as one-way microvalves, letting interstitial fluid enter but preventing its backflow — a feature not seen in blood capillaries.
questions.keyConcept: Overlapping endothelial folds act as one-way valves in lymphatic capillaries.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which is TRUE about conducting arteries?
questions.explanation: Conducting arteries (the aorta and its major branches) are classified histologically as elastic arteries, in contrast to muscular (distributing) arteries such as the radial artery.
questions.keyConcept: Conducting arteries = elastic arteries.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following blood vessel is characterized by presence of amorphous intercellular substance, fat droplets, monocytes and longitudinal smooth muscle fibers in its tunica intima?
questions.explanation: Coronary arteries show a distinctive intimal cushion containing amorphous ground substance, fat droplets, monocytes, and longitudinally oriented smooth muscle fibers, an early substrate relevant to coronary atherosclerosis.
questions.keyConcept: Coronary artery intima has a distinctive musculo-elastic cushion.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following blood vessel, its tunica media contains inner longitudinal and outer circular smooth muscle fibers?
questions.explanation: The coronary artery media is distinctively arranged in two smooth muscle layers: an inner longitudinal layer and an outer circular layer.
questions.keyConcept: Coronary media: inner longitudinal, outer circular smooth muscle.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following blood vessel its wall shows two layers of circularly arranged smooth muscle fibers in the media and thin adventitia?
questions.explanation: Muscular venules are the first venous segment to acquire a true, organized media, consisting of two circular smooth muscle layers, together with a thin adventitia.
questions.keyConcept: Muscular venules have two circular smooth muscle layers in the media.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following cell types truly describes the pericytes?
questions.explanation: Pericytes are commonly described as multipotent mesenchymal progenitor-like cells because they can generate several related mesenchymal lineages under appropriate conditions. “Pluripotent” would imply the much broader developmental potential of embryonic stem cells.
questions.keyConcept: Pericytes are pluripotent perivascular cells.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following cells secretes collagen fibers of tunica adventitia of blood vessels?
questions.explanation: Fibroblasts residing in the tunica adventitia synthesize the collagen fibers that give the outer vessel wall its tensile strength.
questions.keyConcept: Adventitial collagen is produced by fibroblasts.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following characterizes Aorta?
options: Fenestrated elastic membranes in its media
Few vasa vasorum in the adventitia
questions.explanation: The aorta's tunica media is built of numerous concentric fenestrated elastic membranes (lamellae) interspersed with smooth muscle, an adaptation that allows elastic recoil during diastole.
questions.keyConcept: Aortic media consists of fenestrated elastic lamellae.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following characterizes tunica media of the medium-sized arteries?
questions.explanation: The tunica media of a medium muscular artery contains circumferential smooth-muscle layers plus a variable amount of collagen. Longitudinal smooth muscle is not its characteristic arrangement; the external elastic lamina is usually apparent and the matrix contains proteoglycans.
questions.keyConcept: Tunica media of medium arteries is a smooth-muscle-rich layer bordered by an apparent external elastic lamina.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following collagen fibers is chiefly present in tunica adventitia of aorta?
questions.explanation: As in other vessels, the aorta's adventitia is reinforced predominantly by type I collagen fibers.
questions.keyConcept: Aortic adventitia is dominated by type I collagen.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following collagen fibers is chiefly present in tunica adventitia of blood vessels?
questions.explanation: The tunica adventitia is reinforced predominantly by type I collagen fibers, which resist longitudinal stretch.
questions.keyConcept: Adventitia is dominated by type I collagen.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following filaments help pericytes to regulate blood flow to capillaries?
questions.explanation: Pericytes contain contractile actin and myosin filaments that allow them to constrict or relax around capillaries, helping regulate local capillary blood flow.
questions.keyConcept: Pericyte actin/myosin filaments enable contractile regulation of capillary flow.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following has more frequent vasa vasorum?
questions.explanation: Veins carry lower-oxygen blood and have thinner walls, so medium-sized veins have proportionally more numerous vasa vasorum than arteries of comparable caliber, which rely more on luminal diffusion through fenestrated elastic laminae.
questions.keyConcept: Medium-sized veins have more abundant vasa vasorum than comparable arteries.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following in NOT a characteristic of basilar artery?
options: Thin media with little elastic fibers
Adventitia is thicker than the media
questions.explanation: The basilar artery actually has an adventitia that is thinner than its media, not thicker; its true features are a wide lumen with thin wall, a well-developed internal elastic lamina, a thin media with little elastic tissue, and absence of an external elastic lamina.
questions.keyConcept: The basilar artery's adventitia is thinner than its media.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following is a character of external elastic lamina?
options: It is formed of non-fenestrated elastin sheet.
It is formed of reticular and elastic fibers.
It characterizes the structure of veins.
It separates tunica intima from tunica media.
It is a part of tunica media.
questions.explanation: The external elastic lamina, seen in muscular arteries, forms the outer boundary of the tunica media next to the adventitia and is regarded as part of the media.
questions.keyConcept: External elastic lamina is the outer boundary of the tunica media.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following is a character of internal elastic lamina?
options: It is formed of non-fenestrated elastin sheet.
It is formed of collagen and elastic fibers.
It is present in all types of blood vessels.
It separates tunica intima from tunica media.
It is a part of tunica adventitia.
questions.explanation: The internal elastic lamina is a fenestrated elastin sheet that marks the boundary between the tunica intima and tunica media in arteries.
questions.keyConcept: Internal elastic lamina marks the intima/media boundary.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following is a part of vasa vasorum?
questions.explanation: Vasa vasorum are themselves networks of small vessels (arterioles, capillaries, and venules) that penetrate the adventitia and outer media of large vessels to nourish the wall.
questions.keyConcept: Vasa vasorum are made up of arterioles, capillaries, and venules.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following is characterized by the presence of blood sinusoids?
questions.explanation: The spleen (along with liver, bone marrow, and some endocrine glands) is supplied by blood sinusoids, wide irregular vascular channels with a discontinuous wall suited to filtering blood cells.
questions.keyConcept: The spleen is supplied by blood sinusoids.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following is characterized by the presence of continuous capillaries?
questions.explanation: Skeletal muscle (along with brain, connective tissue, and lung) is supplied by continuous capillaries, which have an uninterrupted endothelium suited to tightly regulated exchange.
questions.keyConcept: Skeletal muscle is supplied by continuous capillaries.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following is characterized by the presence of fenestrated capillaries?
questions.explanation: Endocrine glands (along with the kidney and intestinal mucosa) are supplied by fenestrated capillaries, which permit rapid exchange of hormones and small molecules.
questions.keyConcept: Endocrine glands are supplied by fenestrated capillaries.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of medium-sized veins?
questions.explanation: Medium-sized veins do have vasa vasorum (in fact proportionally more than comparable arteries) supplying their thick adventitia; they show a thin subendothelial layer and no internal or external elastic lamina.
questions.keyConcept: Medium-sized veins possess vasa vasorum despite their thin media.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a part of tunica media of aorta?
questions.explanation: The internal elastic lamina marks the boundary between intima and media rather than being a true constituent of the media itself, whereas smooth muscle, elastic, collagen, and reticular fibers are all found within the aortic media.
questions.keyConcept: Internal elastic lamina is a boundary marker, not a medial component.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following is the most characteristic feature of coronary arteries?
options: Fragmented internal elastic lamina in old age.
Adventitia contains collagen and elastic fibers
Media contains smooth muscle fibers in three directions
questions.explanation: With advancing age, the internal elastic lamina of the coronary arteries characteristically becomes fragmented/split, a feature considered most distinctive of these vessels.
questions.keyConcept: Coronary artery internal elastic lamina fragments with age.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following is the thickest layer in the wall of a medium-sized artery?
questions.explanation: In medium-sized (muscular) arteries the tunica media, built of many circularly arranged smooth muscle layers, is the thickest of the three tunicae, reflecting its role in regulating vessel tone and blood pressure.
questions.keyConcept: Media is the thickest tunica in medium-sized arteries.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following is the thickest layer in the wall of a medium-sized vein?
questions.explanation: Unlike arteries, medium-sized veins have a thin media with few smooth muscle layers; the tunica adventitia, rich in collagen, is their thickest layer and provides most of the structural support.
questions.keyConcept: Adventitia is the thickest tunica in medium-sized veins.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following structure can differentiate the continuous capillaries from the fenestrated ones?
options: Endothelial cells are joined by tight junctions
questions.explanation: Continuous capillaries are distinguished by an uninterrupted, complete endothelial cell wall with no fenestrae, unlike fenestrated capillaries, which have circular perforations.
questions.keyConcept: Continuous capillaries have an uninterrupted endothelial wall.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following structure can differentiate the fenestrated capillaries from the continuous ones?
options: Endothelial cells are joined by tight junctions
Endothelial cells show numerous pinocytotic vesicles.
questions.explanation: The defining feature of fenestrated capillaries is the presence of circular perforations (fenestrae) through the endothelial cytoplasm, which continuous capillaries lack.
questions.keyConcept: Fenestrated capillaries have circular endothelial fenestrae/pores.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following structures are NOT present in the tunica intima of the medium-sized artery?
questions.explanation: The tunica intima itself is avascular and depends on diffusion from the lumen and fenestrae in the internal elastic lamina for nourishment; true blood capillaries are not found within it, unlike the endothelium and subendothelial connective tissue that are present.
questions.keyConcept: The tunica intima is avascular and lacks its own blood capillaries.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following structures help in rapid exchange of tissue fluid through fenestrated capillaries?
questions.explanation: The fenestrae (pores) of the endothelial cells provide a direct pathway allowing rapid bulk exchange of fluid and small solutes across fenestrated capillaries.
questions.keyConcept: Fenestrae allow rapid bulk exchange across fenestrated capillaries.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following structures helps the material transport between both luminal and peripheral surface of blood capillaries?
questions.explanation: Pinocytotic vesicles shuttle fluid, macromolecules, and small particles across the endothelial cytoplasm between the luminal (blood) side and the abluminal (tissue) side of the capillary wall.
questions.keyConcept: Pinocytotic vesicles mediate transcytosis across capillary endothelium.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following structures is a part of the tunica intima?
questions.explanation: The tunica intima consists of endothelium plus a thin layer of subendothelial connective tissue (and internal elastic lamina in arteries); vasa vasorum, external elastic lamina, and smooth muscle belong to outer layers.
questions.keyConcept: Tunica intima = endothelium + subendothelial connective tissue.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following structures is NOT a characteristic of arterioles?
options: Absent internal elastic lamina in small arterioles
questions.explanation: Arterioles lack an external elastic lamina altogether; they show a thin subendothelial layer, may lack an internal elastic lamina when very small, and have a thin media and thin adventitia.
questions.keyConcept: Arterioles have no external elastic lamina.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following structures is responsible for nourishment of deep layers of vessel wall?
questions.explanation: Large vessel walls are too thick to be nourished by diffusion from the lumen alone; small nutrient vessels called vasa vasorum penetrate the outer media and adventitia to supply them.
questions.keyConcept: Vasa vasorum nourish the outer layers of large vessel walls.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following structures of medium-sized artery is responsible for control of blood supply to different regions of the body?
questions.explanation: The smooth muscle within the tunica media of medium (muscular) arteries can contract or relax, redistributing blood flow to different vascular beds as needed.
questions.keyConcept: Medial smooth muscle regulates regional blood flow.

questions.chapterTitle: Anatomy and Structure of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Which of the following structures share in transport of substance to and from continuous capillaries?
questions.explanation: Because continuous capillaries have no fenestrae, exchange across their endothelium relies heavily on pinocytotic (pinocytic) vesicles to ferry material between the lumen and surrounding tissue.
questions.keyConcept: Pinocytic vesicles mediate exchange across continuous capillaries.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Nitrates reduce work done by heart in angina mainly through:
options: Redistribution of blood to subendocardial ischemic areas
Vasodilation of stenosed large epicardial coronary arteries & collaterals
Vasodilation of venules with reduction of venous return & preload
questions.explanation: Nitrates act mainly as venodilators, pooling blood in the venous system, reducing venous return and preload, thereby lowering cardiac work. a) Reducing heart rate - FALSE, nitrates can cause reflex tachycardia rather than HR reduction. b) Redistribution of blood to subendocardial ischemic areas - TRUE but not the main mechanism; it is a contributory effect. c) Vasodilation of stenosed large epicardial coronary arteries & collaterals - TRUE but secondary; main effect is on venous side. d) Vasodilation of venules with reduction of venous return & preload - TRUE and MAIN, this primarily reduces myocardial oxygen demand.

questions.text: Reduction of heart rate by beta blockers in angina DO NOT:

Decreases diastolic period resulting in increased coronary filling in diastole
Reduces reflex tachycardia and worsening of angina by nitrates
questions.explanation: By reducing heart rate, ß-blockers prolong, not shorten, diastole, thereby improving coronary filling; a decrease in diastolic period is incorrect. a) Blunts the increase in heart rate & blood pressure during exercise - TRUE, this is a key bene t. b) Controls heart rate at rest (50- 60/min) - TRUE, resting HR control is a target. c) Decreases diastolic period resulting in increased coronary filling in diastole - FALSE, HR reduction increases diastolic period and coronary filling. d) Reduces reflex tachycardia and worsening of angina by nitrates - TRUE, B-blockers blunt nitrate-induced reflex tachycardia.

questions.text: Baroreceptors of carotid sinus and aortic arch are more sensitive to:
questions.explanation: Baroreceptors adapt to static pressure (“Resetting”). They are much more sensitive to dynamic changes and the rate of rise. questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: Blood pressure increases and heart rate decreases in response to:
questions.explanation: Cushing Reflex: High intracranial pressure forces BP to rise (to perfuse the brain). The baroreceptors detect this high systemic BP and reflexly slow the heart. Result: High BP + Low HR. a) Exercise - FALSE because Exercise causes an increase in both heart rate and blood pressure. b) Increased body temperature - FALSE because This typically causes an increase in heart rate. d) Hemorrhage - FALSE because Hemorrhage causes a decrease in blood pressure and an increase in heart rate.

questions.text: In capillary fluid shift:
options: Increase blood pressure leads to more reabsorption at capillaries.
Decrease in blood pressure leads to less capillary filtration.
questions.explanation: Low BP lowers capillary hydrostatic pressure. This favors Reabsorption (Fluid Shift) from tissue to blood to restore volume. a) Increase blood pressure leads to more reabsorption at capillaries - FALSE because Increased BP increases capillary hydrostatic pressure, favoring filtration, not reabsorption. b) It affects the vascular capacity - FALSE because Capillary fluid shift affects blood volume, while vascular capacity is affected by stress relaxation. c) Is increased by sympathetic activity - FALSE because Sympathetic activity primarily constricts arterioles, which can decrease capillary hydrostatic pressure and thus affect filtration, but it doesn't directly "increase" the fluid shift mechanism itself.

questions.text: In response to an increase in blood pressure, baroreceptor effects include.

Stimulation of respiratory center and hyperventilation.

questions.text: Regarding cardiovascular regulatory mechanisms, which is false.
options: Circulating vasoconstrictors hormones include angiotensin Il and aldosterone
Depressor vasomotor control is stimulated by the Baroreceptors
Increased Baroreceptor activation slows down the HR
The vasomotor area is stimulated by hypoxia and hypercapnia
questions.explanation: Aldosterone is not itself a direct vasoconstrictor; it regulates blood volume by promoting renal Na+ (and water) retention. Angiotensin II and vasopressin (ADH) are the true circulating vasoconstrictor hormones, so grouping aldosterone with them as a "circulating vasoconstrictor hormone" is the false statement. The remaining statements are correct: depressor vasomotor control is indeed stimulated by baroreceptors, increased baroreceptor activation does slow the heart rate (via the cardiac vagal center), and the vasomotor area is genuinely stimulated by hypoxia and hypercapnia.

questions.text: The effects of TPR on blood pressure:

Has no marked effect on blood pressure.

questions.explanation: Total Peripheral Resistance (TPR) acts as a “dam.” Increasing TPR traps blood in the arterial tree during diastole, significantly elevating Diastolic Pressure (and Mean Pressure). a) Occurs normally through change in blood viscosity - FALSE because The primary regulator of TPR is the radius of arterioles, not blood viscosity. b) Has no marked effect on blood pressure - FALSE because TPR is a major determinant of mean arterial pressure. d) Changes in radius of blood vessels is directly related to changes in TPR - FALSE because Resistance is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the radius (R is inversely proportional to r^4).

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: The intermediate-term regulation of blood pressure:
options: Includes stress relaxation and capillary fluid shift.
questions.explanation: Intermediate-term blood pressure regulation (minutes to hours) includes stress-relaxation of vessel walls and capillary fluid shift, which adjust vascular capacity and blood volume. Renal and hormonal mechanisms (the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, for example) are classified as long-term regulators, not intermediate-term, which makes that statement false. Nervous (baroreceptor) mechanisms are short-term, not intermediate-term or life-saving in the sense implied here, so those statements are also false; only "includes stress relaxation and capillary fluid shift" correctly describes an intermediate-term mechanism.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: Which of the following hormones is increased in conditions of increase blood pressure:
questions.explanation: Atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) is released from atrial myocytes in response to atrial stretch, which occurs with increased blood volume/pressure; it lowers blood pressure by promoting natriuresis (Na+ excretion) and vasodilation, so it is the hormone that rises with increased volume/pressure. Angiotensin II and aldosterone are released in response to LOW blood pressure or volume (via the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone axis), and antidiuretic hormone is released in response to low blood pressure or increased plasma osmolarity, so all three move in the opposite direction.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: Compare between atrial type "A" and type "B" baroreceptors.
questions.modelAnswer:
| Feature | High-pressure receptors (atrial type A, ventricular, and pulmonary receptors, together with the arterial baroreceptors) | Low-pressure receptors (atrial type B receptors) |
|---|---|---|
| Main stimulus | A rise in arterial blood pressure | A large increase in venous return / blood volume |
| Reflex response | Reflex vasodilatation of peripheral arterioles, bradycardia, and reduced myocardial contractility | Reflex vasodilatation, decreased ADH secretion, and increased atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) secretion, causing vasodilatation of afferent glomerular arterioles and increased urine formation |
| Regulatory role | Share in short- and intermediate-term regulation of arterial blood pressure | Share in long-term regulation of blood volume and arterial blood pressure |
| Additional note | May also act in the pulmonary circulation, lowering ABP and heart rate during a sudden rise in pulmonary pressure | Not applicable |

questions.modelAnswer:
- Components: nucleus ambiguus and dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus.
- When ABP is increased: the activity of the depressor area is enhanced and the pressor area is inhibited, decreasing vasoconstrictor discharge in sympathetic nerves, causing vasodilatation of arterioles and a drop in ABP.
- When ABP is decreased (as in hemorrhage): the activity of the pressor area is enhanced and the depressor area is inhibited, increasing the frequency of vasoconstrictor discharge in sympathetic nerves, accentuating vasomotor tone in arterioles and raising ABP.
- Direct stimuli of the vasomotor center (VMC): hypercapnia, hypoxia, and a marked increase in ABP in cases of increased intracranial tension.

questions.text: Arteriolar smooth muscle in what tissue tends to have beta2 receptors?
questions.explanation: Skeletal-muscle (and, to a lesser extent, hepatic) arterioles carry beta-2 adrenergic receptors. Low circulating levels of epinephrine preferentially bind these beta-2 receptors, causing vasodilation that increases blood flow to skeletal muscle in preparation for a fight-or-flight response. Cerebral vessels are regulated mainly by local metabolic factors rather than beta-2 receptors; cutaneous and gastrointestinal vessels are dominated by alpha-receptor-mediated vasoconstriction; and although the liver has some beta-2 receptors, skeletal muscle is the classic teaching example.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: A pregnant hypertensive patient should NOT receive:
questions.explanation: ACEIs and ARBs are contraindicated in pregnancy, and thiazides are not favored as first-line in pregnant hypertension where methyldopa, labetalol, and CCBs are preferred. a) Thiazides - TRUE, they are not drugs of choice in pregnancy. b) Captopril - TRUE, ACEIs are fetotoxic and contraindicated. c) Candesartan - TRUE, ARBs are contraindicated in pregnancy. d) All of the above - TRUE, all listed drugs should be avoided.
questions.keyConcept: Cardiovascular drugs are chosen by their molecular target, hemodynamic effect, clinical indication, and adverse-effect profile.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: All regarding the side effects of Verapamil are correct EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Verapamil commonly causes constipation, bradycardia, AV block, and may worsen heart failure due to its negative inotropic and dromotropic effects. a) Heart failure - TRUE, because the negative inotropic effect can aggravate pre-existing heart failure. b) Bradycardia - TRUE, due to depression of SA-node automaticity. c) Heart block - TRUE, because it slows AV-node conduction and may precipitate AV block. d) Diarrhea - FALSE, since verapamil typically causes constipation, not diarrhea.
questions.keyConcept: Cardiovascular drugs are chosen by their molecular target, hemodynamic effect, clinical indication, and adverse-effect profile.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Beta blockers & calcium channel blockers do NOT share the following indication:
questions.explanation: CCBs are used in peripheral vascular disease, whereas -blockers are relatively contraindicated as they may worsen vasospasm. a) Angina - TRUE, both B-blockers and CCBs are used in angina. b) Hypertension - TRUE, both classes are major antihypertensives. c) Supra ventricular arrhythmia - TRUE, non-DHP CCBs and B-blockers are used. d) Peripheral vascular diseases - FALSE as shared; CCBs are preferred, B-blockers are generally avoided.
questions.keyConcept: Cardiovascular drugs are chosen by their molecular target, hemodynamic effect, clinical indication, and adverse-effect profile.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Hypotension, heart failure, bradycardia & heart block are side effects of:
questions.explanation: Non-DHP CCBs such as verapamil produce cardiac depression with bradycardia, AV block, hypotension and may worsen heart failure. a) Verapamil - TRUE, it has pronounced negative inotropic and chronotropic actions and can cause these effects. b) Nifedipine - FALSE, DHPs mainly cause vasodilation with reflex tachycardia rather than bradycardia/heart block. c) Amlodipine - FALSE, it is vasoselective with minimal direct cardiac depression. d) Nicardipine - FALSE, as a DHP it primarily causes vasodilation and reflex tachycardia, not marked bradycardia or heart block.
questions.keyConcept: Cardiovascular drugs are chosen by their molecular target, hemodynamic effect, clinical indication, and adverse-effect profile.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: In a diabetic hypertensive patient, the least preferred drug is:
questions.explanation: In diabetic hypertensive patients, nonselective beta blockers like propranolol are less preferred because they may mask hypoglycemia and worsen metabolic control, while ACEIs and ARBs are favored and low-dose thiazides acceptable. a) Low dose thiazides - TRUE, they are acceptable and commonly used at low doses in hypertension, including diabetes, if monitored. b) Propranolol - FALSE, as it is the least preferred due to adverse metabolic and hypoglycemia- masking effects. c) Lisinopril - TRUE, ACEIs are preferred in hypertension with diabetes and nephropathy. d) Candesartan - TRUE, ARBs are good alternatives to ACEIs in diabetic hypertension.
questions.keyConcept: Cardiovascular drugs are chosen by their molecular target, hemodynamic effect, clinical indication, and adverse-effect profile.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The following is WRONG:
options: Trimetazidine is an antianginal that increases myocardial glucose metabolism
Ivabradine is an antianginal that selectively inhibits pacemaker If current
Ranolazine Increase late inward Na current
Tolerance to nitrates is avoided by allowing an 8 hr/day nitrate free period
questions.explanation: Ranolazine actually inhibits the late phase of the Na+ current, reducing Na+ and Ca2+ overload. a) Trimetazidine is an antianginal that increases myocardial glucose metabolism - TRUE, it shifts metabolism from FFA oxidation to glucose, reducing O2 demand. b) Ivabradine is an antianginal that selectively inhibits pacemaker I, current - TRUE, this is its described mechanism. c) Ranolazine Increase late inward Na current - FALSE, it inhibits the late Na+ current, improving diastolic function. d) Tolerance to nitrates is avoided by allowing an 8 hr/day nitrate free period - TRUE, an 8-hour nitrate-free interval is recommended.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The least likely antihypertensive mechanism of amlodipine is:
options: Peripheral arterial vasodilatation and decreased peripheral resistance
Diuretic action due to increased renal blood flow
Decreased aldosterone secretion preventing fluid retention
questions.explanation: Amlodipine primarily causes peripheral arterial vasodilatation and has mild diuretic and aldosterone-suppressing effects, but it does not significantly slow heart rate (often causes reflex tachycardia). a) Peripheral arterial vasodilatation and decreased peripheral resistance - TRUE, this is its main action. b) Negative chronotropic effects - FALSE, it has minimal direct HR slowing and may cause reflex tachycardia. c) Diuretic action due to increased renal blood flow - TRUE, CCBs increase renal blood flow and have a mild diuretic effect. d) Decreased aldosterone secretion preventing fluid retention - TRUE, decreased aldosterone helps prevent edema.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: The main mechanism of antihypertensive action of beta blockers is:
questions.explanation: Beta blockers lower blood pressure mainly by blocking ß1 receptors in juxtaglomerular cells, decreasing renin, angiotensin II, and aldosterone. a) Negative inotropic & chronotropic effects - FALSE, they directly reduce cardiac output and blood pressure but it's not the main antihypertensive mechanism, it's the second main mechanism. b) Suppression of renin release - TRUE, main antihypertensive mechanism. c) resetting of baroreceptors - FALSE as "main"; it is an additional long-term effect. d) Central & peripheral sympatholytic effect - FALSE as "main"; this is supportive rather than primary.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Thiazide diuretics do NOT exhibit the following characteristic:
options: High dose induces more hypotensive effect than low dose
Long-term hypotensive effect of thiazides is due to vasodilator effect
Initial hypotensive effect is secondary to an increase in cardiac output & extracellular volume
They are useful in hypertension associated with osteoporosis
questions.explanation: The text emphasizes low-dose thiazides give effective BP control with fewer metabolic effects; increasing dose mainly increases side effects, not hypotension. a) Synergize with most antihypertensive drugs - TRUE, by reducing volume and RAAS activation. b) High dose induces more hypotensive effect than low dose - FALSE, higher doses mostly add toxicity rather than extra BP fall. c) Long-term hypotensive effect of thiazides is due to vasodilator effect - TRUE, delayed effect is vasodilation. d) Initial hypotensive effect is secondary to an increase in cardiac output & extracellular volume - TRUE, early effect is diuretic. e) They are useful in hypertension associated with osteoporosis - TRUE, they reduce urinary calcium loss.
questions.keyConcept: Cardiovascular drugs are chosen by their molecular target, hemodynamic effect, clinical indication, and adverse-effect profile.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Using Propranolol to treat hypertension, it may cause all the following EXCEPT:
options: May precipitate cardiac failure in susceptible patients
Should be avoided in a patient with 2 Reynaud's phenomenon
questions.explanation: Propranolol may worsen asthma, precipitate heart failure, and is avoided in Raynaud's, but postural hypotension is more typical with a-blockers than with ß-blockers. a) May exacerbate asthma - TRUE, nonselective ß-blockade can trigger bronchospasm. b) Often produces postural hypotension - FALSE, this is not a characteristic major effect of 17 propranolol. c) May precipitate cardiac failure in susceptible patients - TRUE, due to negative inotropy. d) Should be avoided in a patient with Reynaud's phenomenon - TRUE, because it can worsen peripheral vasoconstriction.
questions.keyConcept: Cardiovascular drugs are chosen by their molecular target, hemodynamic effect, clinical indication, and adverse-effect profile.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which of the following statements is CORRECT concerning thiazides:
options: Metolazone is ineffective in patients with renal impairment
Long term antihypertensive effect results from reduction of blood volume
Beta blockers are preferred to thiazides in isolated systolic hypertension
Indapamide induces less metabolic side effects
questions.explanation: The text highlights low-dose thiazide-like drugs such as indapamide as preferred and notes that low doses are not associated with metabolic adverse effects, so indapamide has fewer metabolic problems. a) Metolazone is ineffective in patients with renal impairment - FALSE, metolazone is actually useful in resistant hypertension with renal impairment. b) Long term antihypertensive effect results from reduction of blood volume - FALSE, the delayed effect is due to vasodilation, not continued volume loss. c) Beta blockers are preferred to thiazides in isolated systolic hypertension - FALSE, thiazides/ CCBs are preferred in isolated systolic hypertension. d) Indapamide induces less metabolic side effects - TRUE, low-dose thiazide-like diuretics such as indapamide are noted to have minimal metabolic effects.
questions.keyConcept: Cardiovascular drugs are chosen by their molecular target, hemodynamic effect, clinical indication, and adverse-effect profile.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect concerning antihypertensives:
options: Hydralazine is used in pre-eclampsia as a second choice to labetalol
Alpha-methyl dopa is of choice in pregnancy
Thiazides are preferred in uncomplicated hypertension
Labetalol is used in hypertensive crisis with acute heart failure
questions.explanation: Labetalol is avoided in heart failure according to the hypertensive emergencies section, whereas it is used in hypertensive emergencies without HF; hydralazine is second choice in eclampsia and methyldopa is of choice in pregnancy, and thiazides are preferred in uncomplicated hypertension. a) Hydralazine is used in pre-eclampsia as a second choice to labetalol - TRUE, hydralazine is listed as second choice in eclampsia when others fail. b) Alpha-methyl dopa is of choice in pregnancy - TRUE, methyldopa is a drug of choice in pregnancy. c) Thiazides are preferred in uncomplicated hypertension - TRUE, thiazides are preferred in uncomplicated cases. d) Labetalol is used in hypertensive crisis with acute heart failure - FALSE, labetalol should be avoided in heart failure; other agents like nitroprusside are preferred.

questions.chapterTitle: Special Circulations and Diseases of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Histology
questions.text: Compare blood and lymphatic capillaries.
questions.modelAnswer:
- Blood capillaries: form continuous circuits between arterioles and venules, have relatively narrow lumina, and usually possess a continuous basal lamina with associated pericytes.
- Lymphatic capillaries: begin as blind-ended tubes, have wider and more irregular lumina, show overlapping endothelial flaps that act as one-way valves, have a discontinuous or absent basal lamina, lack pericytes, and are held open by anchoring filaments; they collect excess interstitial fluid and return it to the venous circulation via the lymphatic system.
questions.explanation: A complete answer should identify the relevant microscopic structures and connect each structural feature to its function in cardiac muscle, blood vessels, capillaries, or lymphatics.
questions.keyConcept: Accurate cardiovascular histology depends on relating microscopic organization to mechanical, conductive, exchange, or drainage function.

questions.text: factor does NOT increase lymph flow:
options: Rhythmic contraction of the wall of large ducts.
questions.explanation: increasing plasma proteins raises capillary oncotic pressure, which pulls more fluid from the interstitium back into the bloodstream. This reduces interstitial fluid volume, the very source of lymph, thereby decreasing lymph flow. a) Rhythmic contraction of the wall of large ducts. - FALSE because this intrinsic “lymphatic - pump” is a primary mechanism that actively propels lymph forward. b) Skeletal muscle contraction. - FALSE because the external “muscle pump” compresses lymph vessels, forcing lymph toward the thoracic duct. c) Arterial pulsations. - FALSE because pulsations from nearby arteries can compress lymphatic vessels, aiding in the movement of lymph.
questions.keyConcept: Lymphatics return excess interstitial fluid and protein to the circulation and support immune and lipid transport.

questions.keyConcept: Lymphatics return excess interstitial fluid and protein to the circulation and support immune and lipid transport.

questions.chapterTitle: Special Circulations and Diseases of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: An increase in which of the following tends to decrease capillary filtration rate?
questions.explanation: an increase in plasma colloid osmotic pressure strengthens the force that pulls fluid back into the capillary from the interstitium, thereby decreasing the net filtration rate. a) Capillary hydrostatic pressure - FALSE because an increase in this pressure would increase the filtration rate. c) Interstitial osmotic pressure - FALSE because an increase in this pressure would pull more fluid 20 out, increasing the filtration rate. d) Venous hydrostatic pressure - FALSE because an increase in venous pressure is transmitted back to the capillaries, increasing capillary hydrostatic pressure and thus filtration. e) Arteriolar diameter - FALSE because arteriolar dilation increases capillary hydrostatic pressure, which increases the filtration rate.
questions.keyConcept: Capillary exchange is governed by hydrostatic and oncotic forces, permeability, local metabolites, and lymphatic drainage.

questions.chapterTitle: Special Circulations and Diseases of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: Given the following information, calculate the net filtration pressure: capillary hydrostatic pressure = 30 mm Hg, interstitial fluid pressure = -2 mm Hg, capillary osmotic pressure = 27 mm Hg, and interstitial fluid osmotic pressure = 5 mm Hg.
questions.explanation: Net Filtration Pressure (NFP) = (Capillary Hydrostatic Pressure + Interstitial Fluid Osmotic Pressure) - (Plasma Osmotic Pressure + Interstitial Fluid Hydrostatic Pressure). Using the values: (30 + 5) - (27 + (-2)) = 35 - 25 = +10 mmHg. A positive NFP favors filtration. a) 40 mm Hg, favoring filtration - FALSE because this value is incorrectly calculated and is too high. b) -40 mm Hg, favoring reabsorption - FALSE because this value is incorrectly calculated and the magnitude is wrong. d) -10 mm Hg, favoring reabsorption - FALSE because the correct calculation gives a positive value, not negative. e) 0 mm Hg, no net force - FALSE because the forces are not balanced in this scenario.
questions.keyConcept: Capillary exchange is governed by hydrostatic and oncotic forces, permeability, local metabolites, and lymphatic drainage.

questions.chapterTitle: Special Circulations and Diseases of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: Regarding capillaries:
options: Characterized by very rapid blood flow.
Have small total cross sectional area.
RBCs diameter is smaller than diameter of most body capillaries.
Dilated capillaries can not tolerate increased pressure, and easily ruptured.
questions.explanation: capillary walls are extremely thin and fragile; dilation increases their radius and thus wall tension (Laplace's Law), making them susceptible to rupture under increased internal pressure. a) Characterized by very rapid blood flow. - FALSE because blood flow through capillaries is characteristically very slow to allow adequate time for exchange of materials. b) Have small total cross sectional area. - FALSE because capillaries have the largest total cross- sectional area of any vessel type, which is why flow velocity is lowest there. c) RBCs diameter is smaller than diameter of most body capillaries. - FALSE because red blood cells are typically larger than the capillary diameter and must deform to pass through in single file.
questions.keyConcept: Capillary exchange is governed by hydrostatic and oncotic forces, permeability, local metabolites, and lymphatic drainage.

questions.chapterTitle: Special Circulations and Diseases of Blood Vessels
questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: The osmotic pressure exerted by ______ in the blood is known as colloid osmotic pressure.
questions.explanation: “colloid” refers to the large protein molecules in plasma (like albumin) that cannot easily cross capillary walls and thus generate a significant osmotic pressure. b) small ions - FALSE because small ions are crystalloids, not colloids; they diffuse easily and do not create a sustained osmotic gradient across capillaries. c) large ions - FALSE because while some ions are large, the term “colloid osmotic pressure” a specifically refers to proteins. d) lipids - FALSE because lipids are transported in lipoproteins or bound to carriers and do not directly contribute to the osmotic pressure in this context. e) steroids - FALSE because steroids are lipid-soluble hormones that diffuse freely across membranes and do not contribute to osmotic pressure.
questions.keyConcept: Capillary exchange is governed by hydrostatic and oncotic forces, permeability, local metabolites, and lymphatic drainage.

options: Vesicular transport for water and minerals.
Filtration, according to the balance between hydrostatic and osmotic pressure gradients.
questions.explanation: bulk flow (filtration and reabsorption) is the movement of fluid across the capillary wall driven by the net balance between hydrostatic and colloid osmotic pressures (Starling forces). a) Vesicular transport for water and minerals. - FALSE because vesicular transport is for large molecules like proteins; water and small solutes move through pores or by diffusion. b) Diffusion, according to pressure gradient. - FALSE because diffusion is driven by concentration gradients, not pressure gradients (which drive bulk flow). d) Diapedesis for lipid soluble substances. - FALSE because diapedesis is the passage of white blood cells through the vessel wall, and lipid-soluble substances diffuse directly through the endothelial cell membranes.

questions.explanation: vasomotion is the intermittent, rhythmic contraction and relaxation of precapillary sphincters, causing blood flow through capillary beds to be alternating and pulsatile. b) Is mainly due to nervous factors. - FALSE because it is primarily controlled by local metabolic and chemical factors (e. g., oxygen, CO2 pH), not the nervous system. c) Is unaffected by tissue metabolites. - FALSE because it is highly sensitive to tissue metabolites; low oxygen or high CO, causes sphincters to relax and open. d) Occurs at a normal rate of 15-20/ minute. - FALSE because the rate of vasomotion is variable and depends on the metabolic needs of the tissue, not a fixed rate.

questions.text: Capillary permeability is:
options: The same in all body capillaries.
Decreased by hypoproteinemia in liver and renal diseases.
Decreased by inflammatory chemical mediators such as toxins and substance P.
Is higher at its venous end than at its arteriolar end.
questions.explanation: Capillary permeability is not uniform: it is higher at the venous end than at the arteriolar end because venous-end endothelial junctions are wider, facilitating exchange and reabsorption. a) The same in all body capillaries - FALSE, permeability varies markedly by tissue (very high in liver sinusoids and renal glomeruli, very low in the brain due to the blood-brain barrier) and along the length of a single capillary. b) Decreased by hypoproteinemia in liver and renal diseases - FALSE, hypoproteinemia does not directly decrease permeability; rather, the resulting low plasma oncotic pressure favors fluid filtration and edema. c) Decreased by inflammatory chemical mediators such as toxins and substance P - FALSE, inflammatory mediators such as histamine and substance P increase capillary permeability, not decrease it.
